newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears digital telecoms network accord.
newsitem.headline: EU clears digital telecoms network accord.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had cleared an agreement between five leading European phone companies to create a digital telecommunications network.

But it warned that it was watching to ensure the companies -- British Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Telecom Italia and Telefonica de Espana -- did not discriminate when leasing lines to competitors.

The move involves an accord between the companies to link their circuits to create the Global European Network (GEN), a high-quality fibre optics network using so-called PDH (plesiosynchronous digital hierarchy) technology.
"This agreement amongst the major European telecommunications operators will considerably improve the quality of trans-European telecommunications services," the European Union said in a statement.
However, it said it would scrutinise all such accords involving dominant operators to ensure they were not anti-competitive.

When it opened the investigation in May 1995, the Commission expressed concern about the prices the phone companies would charge to competitors who wanted to lease lines to set up competing digital networks.

"Should the European Commission become aware that the conditions under which access is provided are discriminatory or excessive, individual cases (under EU competition rules) will be opened against the telecommunications operators in question," the Commission said.

The Commission said it had cleared the deal only after obtaining concessions from the companies, including a pledge that they would not set prices collectively and would negotiate access to GEN capacity on a bilateral basis.
They also agreed that access by third parties to the network would be offered on the same basis as to the GEN participants.
The agreement was originally submitted to the Commission for clearance in August 1993. -- Suzanne Perry, Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
